Per the AI Policy, using AI as a coding tool is welcome, but a high bar is held for all contributions, and contributors (not the AI itself) are expected to be responsible for any code they publish, while project maintainers remain responsible for any code published in a release [concepts/ai-policy.md]. This policy applies to all contributions per the Contributing guidelines [concepts/contributing.md]. There is no specific statement in the provided passages about whether fully autonomous agents (without human oversight/responsibility) are permitted to contribute—that detail is missing from the evidence.

Autonomous agents are explicitly disallowed from contributing to ripgrep: the project requires "a human in the loop who understands the work produced by AI," and states that "autonomous agents are not allowed to be used for contributing to this project" [references/source-002.md]. Pull requests that appear to violate this policy may be closed, potentially without notice [references/source-002.md]. This is distinct from AI use in general—using AI/LLMs as coding tools is welcome, provided contributors remain responsible for the code they submit and maintainers remain responsible for anything published in a release [references/source-002.md]. The project's Contributing guide reinforces this by requiring all AI use in contributions to follow the AI Policy, with non-compliant contributions subject to closure [references/source-004.md].

The FAQ passage only lists "How do I search compressed files?" as a topic heading without giving its content [concepts/faq.md], and the README and GUIDE excerpts do not discuss compressed file searching or a custom decompression mechanism at all [concepts/readme.md][concepts/guide.md][concepts/readme-7.md]. To search compressed files, use ripgrep's `-z/--search-zip` flag, which automatically searches files compressed in common formats—gzip, bzip2, xz, lzma, lz4, Brotli, and Zstd—by shelling out to the corresponding `gzip`, `bzip2`, `xz`, `lz4`, `brotli`, or `zstd` binaries installed on your system [references/source-005.md][references/source-007.md]. For formats not covered by this built-in decompression, ripgrep offers arbitrary input preprocessing filters, which can be used for things like less-supported decompression, PDF text extraction, decrypting, or automatic encoding detection [references/source-007.md].
